exec_path_padding.rule: after the executable path NUL, skip only NUL bytes up to the next pointer (8-byte) boundary of the string area; this is the ONLY alignment-bounded run

post_argv_zero_runs.rule: no length cap on NUL runs after argv; scan the complete bounded post-argv range and evaluate every non-empty string; no environment/apple whitelist and no suffix discard
post_argv_zero_runs.why: userspace zeroes apple strings in place at startup: whole pfz/stack_guard/malloc_entropy strings and the values of ptr_munge/main_stack/th_port, producing runs of ~100+ bytes directly after the environment

public_sources.no_terminator: the first empty string after argv is never an end-of-environment marker; envc is not returned and the env/apple boundary is not provable
public_sources.unavailable_denies: required launcher exports absent or cleared (e.g. by setproctitle clobbering argv+env) -> UNAVAILABLE -> deny; never treat as empty/pass

single_call_truncation.rule: one KERN_PROCARGS2 call; reject when returned_length >= allocation; no size-query recollection
why: with argc requested the kernel reserves the argc word first: buflen = *sizep - sizeof(int)
a truncated response copies the LAST buflen bytes and returns size = buflen + 4 = the allocation exactly, so returned_length < allocation rejects every truncated response
single_call_truncation.nuance_exact_fit: an untruncated response whose argument area is exactly allocation - 4 also returns the allocation and is rejected: a fail-closed false denial to document
single_call_truncation.nuance_arg_max: the kernel returns EINVAL when the requested size minus 4 exceeds ARG_MAX, so the allocation must be <= ARG_MAX + 4 on the target kernel
